patch_description:
The previous program was fundamentally broken: it mutated the DataFrame (added/dropped an "original_index" column, dropped "too distinct" columns, merged columns and re-sorted rows), returned an empty column_orderings list (invalid — the API requires valid per-row orderings), used heavy per-cell attribute-access loops, and its recursion could lose or duplicate rows. Validation failed because the returned shape/data did not preserve the input and the orderings were unusable.

The fix is a complete rewrite that preserves every cell, row and column exactly:
1. Serialize each cell once (missing values -> ""), reusing the string matrix across all candidate constructions.
2. Build 2–3 bounded candidate orderings over column "units" (merged column groups kept adjacent per col_merge): (A) global frequency-ranked order using sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), (C) a length-weighted variant, and (B) a bounded conditional partition tree that picks a leading column per group by length-weighted pair repetition using pre-factorized integer codes, with depth and candidate-column bounds.
3. Score each candidate with the true serial Trie objective (sort serialized rows, sum adjacent longest-common-prefix lengths via C-speed binary search on prefix slices) and return the best.
4. Return the DataFrame with original column labels, each row's values permuted according to its per-row ordering, plus the per-row column-ordering lists (expanded from units), enforcing one_way_dep ordering constraints. Row identity and all stored values are unchanged; only column placement per row changes.
